_note: Real ML Kit line output for a photograph holding TWO complete cards, one above the other, captured 2026-09-02. Both belong to the same person and neither is cropped.
_anonymised: Boxes are exactly as ML Kit reported them, converted from the captured centre-y and height. The person's name, the telephone numbers and the email addresses are replaced by strings of the same shape - same word counts, character classes, lengths and OCR damage, including the lowercase 'l' and capital 'I' the recogniser read for '1' and the comma it read for a full stop. The company addresses are left as printed: they are published business addresses, not a person's.
_source: Samsung SM-G736B, ML Kit text-recognition, Latin. Line angles between 0.0 and +1.8 degrees.
_layout: Upper card, roughly y 1027-1944: a single right-hand column - name, title, address, plus code, two telephones, email, website, then its logo lockup at the foot. Lower card, y 2120-3205: the two-column layout - name and title left, logo lockup right, then full-width contact lines.
_why_it_matters: The §6.4 'several cards per photograph' class, with the two cards stacked rather than side by side. The band between them is 176 pixels of empty space against line heights of 50 to 78 - the horizontal corridor split_cards has to find. Both halves are genuinely whole cards here, so a correct split gives two contacts and any other answer is wrong in a way that is easy to state.
